new_statements.quote: This paper describes the phonology of the Barpak dialect of Ghale (ISO 639-3: ghe) ... The description includes the phoneme inventory, tone, syllable structures, consonant clusters, and both segmental and suprasegmental morphophonological processes, but not stress and intonation. [p.377:] There are five contrastive tones: /55/, /33/, /22/, /21/, and /25/. [p.381:] As in other Tamangish languages (Mazaudon 2005), Barpak Ghale has a word-tone system where the prosodic pattern of a word, formed from a root and bound morphemes, is determined by the root tone.
new_statements.citation: Yoshida, Shigeki. 2024. A phonological sketch of Barpak Ghale. Tokyo University Linguistic Papers (TULIP) 46: 359-393.
new_statements.locator: Abstract p.359; Sec. 5 p.377; Sec. 5.3 p.381

The description includes the phoneme inventory, tone, syllable structures, consonant clusters, and both segmental and suprasegmental morphophonological processes, but not stress and intonation.' (2) Sec. 5 'Tone', the text layerimmediately above the -377- page footer: 'There are five contrastive tones: /55/, /33/, /22/, /21/, and /25/. These tones are represented by Chao tone letters..'. (3) Sec. 5.3 'Tone realization in words', the text layerbetween the -380…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ghale (as described for the Barpak/Southern variety) is a word-tone language with five contrastive tones whose melody is set by the root and spreads over affixes; the author explicitly leaves stress undescribed, and no source gives a word-stress placement rule. Khadgi 2021 (p.74) concurs: tone-bearing unit is the morpheme, focus not marked prosodically.
new_statements.exceptions: Khadgi 2021 p.196 cautions that Nishi reported only four tones for Keura Ghale, so the five-tone analysis 'cannot be automatically assumed for all Ghale varieties'; Nishi 1983:32 (via Khadgi) says breathiness may be relevant in Uiya (Northern) Ghale.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the phonological word (root + atonal affixes/clitics) in Barpak = Southern Ghale (sout2715), NOT a Northern Ghale (nort2709) variety; no accessible source describes Northern Ghale prosody at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Every accessible phonological description of 'Ghale' (Yoshida 2024, Khadgi 2021, Paudel 2008, Nishi 1982) describes the Barpak or Keura varieties, which Glottolog/Ethnologue/Webster assign to Southern Ghale (sout2715, ISO ghe); the quoted tonal statement is therefore a catalog candidate for sout2715, not for nort2709. Northern Ghale proper (Uiya, Sirdibas/Jagat, Philim, Nyak, Korla) has only unpublished SIL mimeographs (Seaward 1972-75, 1994), Webster's 1992/2022 survey, and Smith 1999 (destroyed). Khadgi 2021:5 and Yoshida 2026 note the Northern/Southern split itself is inconclusive (Barpak speakers report understanding other villages; lexical similarity Barpak-Uiya ~74-83% per Webster 1992).

sources.note: Barpak (Southern Ghale). Sec. 4.2 p.74: 'In Barpak Ghale, the tone-bearing unit is the morpheme..'; five contrastive tones; Sec. 4.5: focus 'is not marked with any intonational or other prosodic means'.
